title: Display readable rate-limit errors in the signup form
prompt:
Fix unreadable errors in the homepage signup form. Evidence: src/components/WaitlistForm.tsx:26-28 assigns data.error directly to the message state, and lines 61-64 render that value. The rate-limit response uses a boolean error flag plus a string message. A local execution with HTTP 429 and {error:true,message:"Try again in 60 seconds."} stored boolean true as the message; React renders that as no text. Users cannot tell why signup failed or when to retry.

Change only src/components/WaitlistForm.tsx in production. Normalize unsuccessful response bodies to readable text: prefer a nonempty string message, otherwise a nonempty string error, otherwise the existing generic fallback. Never put booleans, arrays, or objects into the rendered message. Handle null bodies safely. Preserve the entered email on failure, leave the button available for retry, and preserve existing successful signup behavior. This is separate from open PR #39, which changes server-side email validation.

Add exactly one new test file, tests/waitlist-error-message.test.ts. Execute the real component with TypeScript transpilation and mocked React hooks, JSX, and fetch; submit only fixture data through the stub. Cover boolean error with message, string error, object error, null body, missing message, network rejection, and successful signup. Assert visible text, preserved email, and retry availability. Run node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/waitlist-error-message.test.ts. Use existing dependencies only. No credentials, deploys, real sends, payments, migrations, workflows, package.json, or auth changes. Do not commit or push; work on the assigned branch you are on.
